standard.title: Media arts across cultures and contexts
standard.description: explore where, why and how people across cultures, communities and/or other contexts experience media arts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify arts works in their own lives and explain why they matter to people. They have not yet explored media arts works across different cultures or communities, or considered the roles and responsibilities of media artists.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can explore where, why and how people across cultures, communities and/or other contexts experience media arts, and describe the role of media artists and what permissions mean.

nodes.label: Media arts across contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify where they encounter media arts works in their lives and communities — naming types of media and contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different types of media arts works encountered in their own life and explain where and when they experience each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of media types and contexts (podcasts, animated shows, advertisements, games, news) encountered in school, home and community settings; describe the purpose of each type; ask Viewpoints questions: 'What story is this work telling?', 'Who made this?', 'Where is it from?'
wider: Compare media arts works encountered at home vs at school vs in the community — investigating how different contexts produce different types of media and different audience experiences
Investigate how media arts works in different cultural contexts (e.g. animated shows from different countries) communicate cultural knowledge and community values
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot identify the range of media contexts they inhabit, the 'across cultures and communities' exploration has no concrete grounding — subsequent questions about purpose and meaning have no examples to work from.

response_modes.reason: Vary the media contexts encountered — podcasts, animated shows, advertisements, games, news — so students develop a broad understanding of what counts as media arts, not just the forms most familiar to them.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least two types of media arts works from their own life
Student can describe where and when they encounter each type

nodes.label: Purpose and cultural knowledge
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why a media arts work was made and how it communicates cultural knowledge — connecting purpose to content and form.
nodes.minimum_width: Choose one media arts work and explain: who made it, what community it comes from, and what cultural knowledge or story it communicates.
nodes.typical_width: Explore media arts works from different cultural contexts and communities; use Viewpoints questions to investigate purpose and cultural knowledge ('Who made this work?', 'What story is it telling?', 'Where is it from?'); discuss how media arts works celebrate cultural knowledge in their own and other communities.
wider: Investigate how media arts works in students' own community communicate and celebrate cultural knowledge — for example, through podcasts, animated children's shows, or community news bulletins
Compare how the same cultural event (e.g. a community celebration) might be communicated differently through different media forms — discussing what each form can and cannot communicate

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions explicitly as a structured inquiry frame — 'Who?', 'Where?', 'What story?' — to build transferable critical viewing skills.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The variety of cultural contexts available at Y1-2 for media arts exploration (First Nations, local community, international animation) is genuinely rich — students who investigate across contexts develop much stronger critical media literacy.
success_criteria: Student can identify who made a media arts work and what community it comes from
Student can describe what cultural knowledge or story the work communicates

nodes.label: Roles and responsibilities of media artists
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the role of media artists and explain what permission means in relation to using and sharing images, sounds and text.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one role a media artist plays (e.g. photographer, animator, filmmaker) and explain one permission consideration for using images or sounds created by others.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the roles of media artists across different types of media; develop class rules for using and creating images, sounds and text; apply permission principles to their own creation and sharing activities; understand that some cultural material belongs to a group rather than an individual.
wider: Develop a class set of rules for using and creating images, sounds and text in media arts — drawing on media artist role examples and permission principles to ground each rule in a real scenario

Investigate a specific case of permission in context: obtaining permission to share a class story as a news bulletin, understanding that permission from individuals and from cultural groups may be different

response_modes.reason: Connecting media artist roles to permission responsibilities integrates the 'what people do' with the 'what they owe' — support students in seeing permission as an ethical dimension of the media artist's role, not a separate compliance requirement.

success_criteria: Student can describe at least one role a media artist plays
Student can explain what permission means in at least one media context (e.g. taking photos of people, using someone else's music)
